ic_name: MIPI DSI v1.01.00 (Display Serial Interface, MIPI Alliance)
powerup_sequence: 1. Power applied — t_POR elapses while host POR is asserted.
2. Host drives sustained LP-11 TX-Stop on all Lanes for T_INIT_MASTER ≥ t_POR + T_INIT_SLAVE + T_INTERNAL_DELAY of the peripheral.
3. Peripheral powers up in RX-Stop and ignores all Link states for at least T_INIT_SLAVE (R-C timer with ±30% accuracy acceptable).
4. Peripheral T_INIT_SLAVE expires; peripheral Rx state machine becomes active; T_INTERNAL_DELAY may follow if peripheral needs more time before accepting bus transactions.
5. Peripheral's Maximum Return Packet Size is initialized to default value 1.
6. Host issues Set Maximum Return Packet Size Short Packet (DT=0x37) to program desired read-response size.
7. Host issues Turn On Peripheral (DT=0x32) — peripheral exits low-power state and enables display.
8. Host begins normal Video Mode or Command Mode operation.
command_mode_write_sequence: 2. Host issues HS Entry (LP-11 → LP-01 → LP-00 → HS-0 → Sync 8'b00011101).
3. Host transmits DCS Short Write Short Packet — DI (VC + DT=0x05 or 0x15) + DCS Command Byte + parameter byte (or 0x00) + ECC.
4. (Optional) Host appends EoTp Short Packet — DI=0x08 + 0x0F + 0x0F + 0x01.

6. (Optional) Host asserts TurnRequest → BTA. Peripheral acquires bus → sends Acknowledge Trigger Message (0x21) if no errors, or Acknowledge and Error Report (DT=0x02) if any Error Register bits are set → BTA back to host.
command_mode_read_sequence: 1. Host issues DCS Read Short Packet (DT=0x06) in HS mode — DI + DCS Command Byte + 0x00 + ECC.
2. Host asserts TurnRequest after the Read Request packet → BTA escape sequence.
3. Peripheral acquires bus; transmits in LP mode.
4. If no error: peripheral sends requested DCS Short Read Response (DT=0x21 or 0x22) or DCS Long Read Response (DT=0x1C) within bounded length per Set Maximum Return Packet Size.
5. If single-bit ECC error in request: peripheral sends Read Response AND Acknowledge and Error Report Short Packet in same LP transmission, with ECC Single Bit (bit 8) set.
6. If multi-bit ECC error in request: peripheral sends ONLY Acknowledge and Error Report (no read data) with ECC Multi Bit (bit 9) set.
7. Peripheral asserts TurnRequest → BTA escape → host re-acquires bus.
video_mode_frame_sequence_non_burst_sync: 1. Host LP-11 idle, then HS Entry.
2. For each VSA line: Host sends VSS Short Packet (DT=0x01) + BLLP Long Packet (Null DT=0x09 or LP gap) + VSE Short Packet (DT=0x11). Repeat for VSA lines.
3. For each VBP line: Host sends HSS (DT=0x21) + BLLP. Repeat for VBP lines.
4. For each VACT line: HSS + HSA (Blanking Packet, no data, DT=0x19) + HSE (DT=0x31) + HBP (Blanking Packet) + RGB Long Packet (Packed Pixel Stream DT=0x0E/0x1E/0x2E/0x3E) + HFP (Blanking Packet).
5. For each VFP line: HSS + BLLP.
6. End of frame: HS Exit → LP-11 → repeat at next frame.
video_mode_frame_sequence_burst: 1. Host LP-11 idle, then HS Entry.
2. For each VACT line: HSS + HBP + RGB (time-compressed pixel-stream Long Packet) + BLLP (LP gap or Blanking Packet) + HFP.
3. Burst Mode time-compresses RGB to free time for LP transition (saves power) or for other transmissions on the same DSI Link.
4. End of frame: HS Exit → LP-11.
tearing_effect_sequence: 1. Host has previously issued set_tear_on or set_tear_scanline DCS command to enable TE.
2. To collect TE: host gives bus possession to peripheral by asserting TurnRequest WITHOUT an accompanying DSI command transmission.
3. Peripheral acquires bus; waits for the display TE event (e.g. start of vertical blanking).
4. When TE event occurs, peripheral sends LP Escape Mode sequence + trigger message byte 0x5D (LSB-first 10111010).
5. Peripheral returns bus possession to host via BTA.
6. Host may now write the next frame; if TE-wait period expires (≈ one video frame period) without TE, host re-acquires bus and tries again or reports error.
bta_sequence: 1. Host completes last packet of a transmission and asserts TurnRequest to its PHY just before EoT.
2. Host PHY drives BTA command via LP Escape Mode on Data Lane 0.
3. Peripheral PHY recognizes BTA; peripheral asserts internal TurnRequest as input to its Protocol layer.
4. Peripheral transmits LP response packets (Acknowledge / Error Report / Read Response / TE).
5. Peripheral asserts its own TurnRequest after last response packet.
6. Peripheral PHY drives BTA command back to host.
7. Host re-acquires bus; both ends return to LP-11.
ecc_recovery_sequence: 1. Receiver computes Hamming-modified parity over DI + WC LS + WC MS.
2. Receiver XORs computed parity with received ECC[5:0] to form 6-bit syndrome.
3. If syndrome = 0: header is clean; proceed.
4. If syndrome non-zero AND matches one of the 24 single-bit-error syndromes (Table 22 + decoder Table 21): correct the indicated data bit; set Error Report bit 8 (ECC Single Bit).
5. If syndrome non-zero AND does NOT match any single-bit pattern: 2-bit error detected; set Error Report bit 9 (ECC Multi Bit); drop packet AND drop rest of transmission (boundary lost).
6. Reset receiver to wait for next SoT.
checksum_recovery_sequence: 2. For each payload byte, LSB-first: feed bit through CRC shift register using polynomial x^16+x^12+x^5+1 (LSB-first shift form 0x8408).
3. After all payload bytes processed, CRC register contains computed checksum.
4. Receiver compares with received 2-byte Packet Footer (CRC LS Byte first, then CRC MS Byte).
6. If mismatch: set Error Report bit 10 (Checksum Error); host application decides whether to ignore or re-request via higher-layer logic.
contention_recovery_sequence: Case 1 — Both sides initially detect contention: Both PHYs detect LP High Fault or LP Low Fault → LP TX STOP / transition to LP-RX → wait Host-Processor-Wait Timeout → optional Reset Entry → Peripheral Reset Timeout → resume.

Case 2 — Only host initially detects contention: Host PHY detects fault → LP TX STOP → ErrContention='1' notification to protocol → Engine Wait Timeout → optional Reset Entry → Peripheral observes Reset → resets → resume.
Case 3 — Only peripheral initially detects contention: Peripheral PHY detects fault → transitions to LP-RX → waits until host returns to LP-11 → normal transition resumes.
powerdown_or_shutdown_sequence: 2. Host issues Shutdown Peripheral Short Packet (DT=0x22).
3. Peripheral turns off display in a Video Mode display module for power saving.
4. Note: the interface shall remain powered in order to receive the turn-on or wake-up command.
5. Host issues Turn On Peripheral Short Packet (DT=0x32) to bring the display back.
